Loss-of-function mutations in GATA1 disrupt erythropoiesis, leading to anemia and thrombocytopenia in beta-thalassemia-X-linked thrombocytopenia syndrome. GATA1 also interacts with H3-3A, a component of the histone modification machinery. Thus, mutations in GATA1 or related pathways can indirectly affect histone modification, potentially impacting neurodevelopment and contributing to Bryant-Li-Bhoj neurodevelopmental syndrome 1, which is caused by mutations in H3-3A. The convergence occurs at the level of histone modification pathways, influenced by both GATA1 activity and direct H3-3A mutations.
